results.name: Anklet
results.description:
**Collection:** Prehistory and Historical Archeology Dept.

**Inv.-No.:** [UF-4233.1](https://www.online.landessammlungen-noe.at/objects/1033334)

**Material:** Bronze

**Dimensions:** 8,46x7,83cm

**Dating:** 250-161 BCE

The artefact is a bronze anklet with overlapping ends that are thickened at the ends. The ring exhibits a distinctive profile, characterised by an oval outline and a semi-circular cross-section. The appearance of the object is defined by a series of round beads with intermediate ribs. The interior surface is smooth.

This object was digitized through the ‘Kulturerbe digital’ program of the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, Public Service and Sport.

results.name: Anklet
results.description:
**Collection:** Prehistory and Historical Archeology Dept.

**Inv.-No.:** [UF-775.1](https://www.online.landessammlungen-noe.at/objects/1027556)

**Material:** Copper-alloy

**Dimensions:** 9,30 cm

**Dating:** 250-161 BCE

The hollow sheet metal anklet is fitted with a stopper and is characterised by its simple shape. The ends have a ninefold transverse groove, the rest is smooth. Furthermore, according to the excavation publication, the object was originally filled with a light fabric that has survived in fragmentary condition to this day. Following a recent study of anklets with organic fillings from Moravia, it was hypothesised that these fillings were either a glued filling intended to prevent the wearer's ankle from being injured, or that they were the remains left over from the wax moulds used in the manufacturing process.

This object was digitized through the ‘Kulturerbe digital’ program of the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, Public Service and Sport.

results.name: Anklet
results.description:
**Collection:** Prehistory and Historical Archeology Dept.

**Inv.-No.:** [UF-795](https://www.online.landessammlungen-noe.at/objects/1027576)

**Material:** Copper alloy

**Dimensions:** 8,22 cm

**Dating:** 250-161 BCE

A beaded, hollow bronze ankle-ring with a stopper. It was originally filled with a light fabric, the remains of which are still preserved today. On the outside, three round bosses are arranged in a transverse rib pattern. The ends of the bosses are rounded and bulging, which can be attributed to the pressure applied during the moulding process.

This object was digitized through the ‘Kulturerbe digital’ program of the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, Public Service and Sport.

results.name: Jessy
results.description: A high-quality 3D model of a blonde woman with a natural appearance and well-proportioned physique. She is dressed in a sleek, black, stretchy romper with short legs, a V-neck, and a zipper closure. A delicate gold chain is adorned around her neck, gold bracelets on her wrists, and dark, minimalistic anklets. The figure stands barefoot, centered against a smooth, gradient background in shades of gray. The lighting is diffused, studio-style, symmetrically accentuating the textures of the materials and natural skin tones.

results.name: Apulian Red-Figured Lebes Gamikos
results.description: Culture: [Greek](http://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p08m57h7jrk) Material: Ceramic Dims: H 19.3 Accession No: HCM 234 Current Location: The Hunt Museum Limerick. A [Lebes gamikos](http://vocab.getty.edu/page/aat/300265007) is a Greek wedding gift. Its role was to carry the water which was sprinkled over the bride in the ceremony. [Red figure painting](http://vocab.getty.edu/page/aat/300020201) was an invention of the Athenians in the sixth-century BC. South Italian Greek colonies, including [Apulia](http://www.geonames.org/3169778/puglia.html), continued red-figure vase production after its decline in Athens. There are painted scenes on either side of the object. On one, a woman seated on a rock cradles a dish and on the other, a winged Eros, god of love, clutches a mirror in his right hand. Both figures have rounded bodies, necklaces, bracelets and anklets. Eros wears a beaded bandolier. [More](https://www.huntmuseum.com/explore/item/7876ccfb-7f59-3dc7-ade9-982fe92939a2/?s%3Dapulian&pos=1).

results.name: Benin relief plaque
results.description:
Plaque [Af1898,0115.44](https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/E_Af1898-0115-44)

Relief plaque, lost-wax cast in brass. Wide plaque, rectangular in form with side flanges. Background surface decorated with river leaf patterns and stippling. One nail hole at top, one at centre right and one at bottom.

Depicts Oba (said to be Esigie) on horseback, facing front, holding the wrists of two pages. Wears beaded crown with oro protrusion and feather at left side, deep beaded collar, beaded sash worn diagonally across chest, armlets, beaded anklets, and patterned wrap-around skirt. Sits side saddle on horse on patterned saddle-cloth.

Scanned in situ, in the African gallery.

results.description:

Each mold is decorated with the image of a seated male figure, both shown wearing elaborate headdresses, ear ornaments, and a necklace. In one mold, the anklets and feet are visible, while in the other the feet are covered by a skirt or loincloth.

results.name: Toothiana Model
results.description:
Tooth is a part human and part hummingbird hybrid who has fair skin, feathers that make a curved upward style instead of hair and pink eyes.

Instead of clothes, her entire body seems to be covered in small iridescent contour feathers. Around her wrists and ankles there seem to be golden lines that appear to look like golden bracelets and golden anklets, as well as gold feathers on either side of her head for earrings. Tooth also has long, drapery feathers that start at her waist line and end at her knees. They give the appearance of a skirt or dress.

Tooth is a sweet, bubbly, elegant, daring, agile, graceful, charismatic, motherly, smart and a fierce fighter of a Guardian who adores the children of the world.

results.name: Vase
results.description:
Polychrome vase decorated with a scene depicting seven richly attired figures and a glyphic text below the rim, with the glyphs painted in pink. Among the figures, the use of elaborate skirts stands out, some featuring plaques and fringes in a variety of designs and colors. All figures wear headdresses, jewelry, belts, wristbands, anklets, and earflares. Vertical secondary texts are also present.  NAA paste analysis identifies the vessel as originating from Motul de San José, Petén

IDAEH Cultural Property No. 1.2.144.0637

results.name: Bronze Statue from Sumba, UPTD Museum
results.description:
This bronze statue (MAHS-IDN-COL-039-O-0016) comes from West Sumba, Indonesia and is now in the collections of the UPTD Museum in Kupang. It presents a figure of a standing woman (Ina) holding two children, one in each arm, with a large lizard crawling over her left shoulder. She is adorned with arm bands, necklaces, bracelets and anklets. The figure stands on a round pedestal ringed with seven smaller human figurines.

results.name: Vase
results.description:
Incomplete polychrome vase. It features a scene composed of five figures. One individual, shown kneeling in right profile, wears his hair gathered under a turban and a loincloth marked with jaguar spots. He appears to be offering an object to a standing figure depicted richly attired. Behind this central figure rises a vertical column of seven pseudo-glyphs. Further behind stands another individual holding a spear in his left hand and wearing a loincloth decorated with circular motifs. This is followed by a robust figure shown dressed in a loincloth and mantle, holding a tubular artifact. Adjacent to him is a column containing four glyph-like designs positioned at waist level. The final figure carries objects in his hands. He wears a segmented loincloth and rectangular anklets. 
IDAEH Cultural Property No. 16.2.5.0373
www.fundacionrutamaya.org

Special thanks to the staff of La Ruta Maya Foundation for their hard work on this project.

results.name: Seated man with facial decoration
results.description:
Ceramic whistle in the form of a male figure seated with legs crossed in front and hands resting on the knees. The figure displays well-preserved polychromy: the skin is painted in reddish tones, while the jewelry elements show traces of blue pigment. The character wears a decorated-edge loincloth or skirt, wristbands and anklets, as well as a necklace made of small bells. He also wears a headdress made of knotted cloth. The face features scarification designs on the cheeks and around the mouth, which could be mistaken for a beard. This facial decoration may be linked to identity, status, or ritual symbolism.

 IDAEH Cultural Property No. 1.2.144.1411

results.name: Figurine of a seated boy (Tukkata Sia Ka Ban)
results.description:
A terracotta figurine of a seated boy (MAHS-THA-COL-005-O-0011) from the Ban Phraek Collection, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Thailand. It measures 7.60 cm wide x 12.60 cm high, with a 6 cm wide base. It is a boy with a topknot seated with both hands resting on his knees and wearing bracelets and anklets. The statue serves as an offering to spirits as a way to exchange a bad fortune for a good one. It is usually placed at a road junction or afloat over flowing water. The base is broken. Dated 14th – 18th century.

For open-access to our complete dataset of archaeological sites and historical artifacts from the Maldives, Indonesia, and other countries of the region, please visit us at: https://maritimeasiaheritage.cseas.kyoto-u.ac.jp
